title: Documenting a Tradeoff
context: Recording a design decision when a color is intentionally kept
whyItMatters: When a lower-contrast color is kept intentionally, recording the reason makes the decision clear to the people who work with the design next.
learningObjectives: Recognize when contrast constraints can conflict with brand requirements.
Record intentional decisions for development handoff.
Differentiate a documented tradeoff from an ignored issue.
lessonParagraphs: A contrast tool can identify a measured issue, but it cannot know every project constraint. A brand palette or visual hierarchy may shape a decision to keep a color.
Silently ignoring a flagged issue can leave developers unsure whether it was seen or missed. It can also be raised again in a later review.
A documented tradeoff records the issue and the reason for keeping it. In Avene, the accountability loop lets a designer acknowledge an issue and capture a justification for the decision.
Documentation does not change the measured contrast. It makes the choice visible and helps the team understand what was evaluated.

keyTakeaways: Brand requirements and visual hierarchy can create design tradeoffs.
